questions.q: According to this lesson, what should you already recognize about finishing this program before thinking about what comes next?
options: You built a real, defensible piece of work — a full pipeline from raw SQL Server data to a finished Power BI dashboard — and that alone is a complete, hireable milestone
The program isn't actually finished until you pick one of the three advanced directions
None of the technical work you did counts until you earn a certification
You need to immediately specialize before applying to any job
questions.explain: This lesson is explicit that finishing the capstone is a real, complete milestone on its own — the directions covered are for further growth, not a signal that the program's work isn't done.

questions.q: What are the three honest directions this lesson describes for a working BI developer to grow into?
options: Going deeper into the Microsoft BI stack, branching into an adjacent data role, or pursuing a relevant certification
Quitting the field, starting a new unrelated career, or repeating this program
Only becoming a database administrator, with no other options
Immediately pursuing a graduate degree as the sole next step
questions.explain: The three directions are going deeper in the tools you already use, branching into an adjacent data role, and pursuing a certification — and the lesson notes they aren't mutually exclusive.

questions.q: What does a data analyst role typically build on top of, according to this lesson, for someone coming out of this program?
options: Reporting and dashboarding experience from SSRS and Power BI, extended with deeper statistics and forecasting
No overlap at all with anything covered in this program
Only database administration experience
Only experience with cloud pipeline tools
questions.explain: A data analyst role builds on the reporting and dashboarding experience from SSRS and Power BI, adding deeper statistics, forecasting, and business-facing analysis.

questions.q: What does this lesson say about pursuing a certification?
options: It's most worthwhile when it supports a direction you're already leaning toward, and hands-on project experience makes studying for one more concrete — not a substitute for that experience
A certification is required before you can apply to any BI developer job
Certifications should always be pursued before any hands-on project work
Certifications guarantee a specific salary regardless of experience
questions.explain: This lesson frames certifications as most useful once they support a direction you already lean toward, building on real hands-on experience rather than replacing it.

questions.q: According to the lesson's closing guidance, when does this lesson suggest the choice between these directions is easiest to make?
options: Once you're actually working, since the honest answer tends to become clearer with real job experience than it is right after finishing the program
Before starting this program, so the direction is locked in from day one
It must be decided immediately, before applying to any jobs
The choice is permanent and cannot change once made
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly says none of this needs to be decided today, and that the honest answer is almost always clearer once you're actually doing the work.
